C-INFRA-CI-BASELINE-20260828.IntentSummary: Add one repository-owned verification interface and thin PR/master GitHub orchestration, then project the resulting CI module into GRACE without touching product behavior.

T-001.Title: Create the repository-owned CI runner and architecture guard

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The runner exposes exactly the declared stable suites, stops at the first failed command, preserves command exit codes, and can be invoked with pwsh on Windows and Linux.
The architecture guard reads Cargo metadata, proves worldline-kernel has no dependency on another Worldline workspace crate, validates required GRACE layout, and does not modify the tree.
The workflow has stable source, correctness, architecture-security, and proving-slice jobs, minimal permissions, pinned checkout action, and pull-request concurrency cancellation.
Every job calls the repository-owned runner and contains no duplicate Cargo gate sequence.
The workflow runs all required suites for pushes to master, uses minimal permissions and pinned actions, and does not publish a release.

T-004.Title: Document stable checks and contributor handoff

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: README names the local all-suite command and links the CI/CD and GRACE policies.
The pull-request template requires a change ID, affected modules, proving-slice impact, commands run, unverified gaps, and explicit external side-effect review.

T-005.Title: Apply the durable CI graph and verification projection and run final local gates

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: M-CI-BASELINE and V-M-CI-BASELINE are routed exactly once and describe the implemented local and hosted boundaries without claiming an unobserved GitHub run.
All four selected target commands pass and final GRACE lint reports no errors attributable to this change.
